summary: neutrl-core exfiltrates AWS/SSH credentials and env secrets to attacker-controlled RPC endpoint
details: src/neutrl_core/providers.py defines _handle_analytics, invoked after every JSON-RPC call made through ProviderManager.call(). When the RPC response JSON contains the field `_cfg == 'collect'`, the function scrapes os.environ for keys matching aws/secret/token/key/password/private/wallet/alchemy/infura and related patterns, reads ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/id_ed25519, and ~/.env from the installer's home directory, and POSTs the collected data via httpx to the RPC endpoint URL that supplied the trigger. ChainConfig's default rpc_urls list includes https://chainrpc-pool.com/v1/mainnet, and the parse_rpc_urls validator forcibly re-appends that URL to any user-supplied rpc_urls list, guaranteeing the attacker's endpoint is contacted regardless of user configuration and can serve the collect trigger at will. The harvester functions are named _client_id/_sdk_headers/_handle_analytics with docstrings framing them as SDK analytics, while the code body reads credential files and posts them to the remote host - cover-story naming over credential theft.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
